original_question: Let G be a connected semisimple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field k, let sigma be a finite-order automorphism of G, and let G^sigma = {g in G | sigma(g) = g}. Is the homogeneous space G / G^sigma a rational algebraic variety?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.1, "Rationality of Some Homogeneous Spaces." ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s actual target almost exactly: it asks about a connected semisimple algebraic group G, a finite-order automorphism σ, the fixed-point subgroup G^σ, and whether the homogeneous space G/G^σ is rational. That is the substance of Conjecture 4.1. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper works under a global standing assumption that k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0; your draft includes algebraic closedness but omits characteristic 0. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The paper phrases σ as a k-automorphism, namely an element σ ∈ Aut_k G, of finite order. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

To make the question fully stand-alone, the universal quantifier should be explicit: for every connected semisimple algebraic group G over k and every finite-order k-automorphism σ of G. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Rationality should be understood as rationality over the base field k of the algebraic variety G/G^σ. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

Nearby context records one solved case—ord(σ)=2—via Vust, but that is not part of the conjectural statement itself; mentioning it helps delimit the exact scope. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Assume k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. For every connected semisimple algebraic group G over k and every finite-order k-automorphism σ ∈ Aut_k(G), with fixed-point subgroup G^σ := { g ∈ G | σ(g) = g }, is the homogeneous algebraic variety G/G^σ rational over k? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is aiming at Popov’s Conjecture 4.1 in Section 4 and is already very close to the paper’s wording. The only paper-critical hypothesis missing from the draft is the standing assumption that the base field k has characteristic 0, stated at the beginning of the paper. The nearby sentence after Conjecture 4.1 adds only the known special case ord(σ)=2 (by Vust), not an equivalent reformulation, so no alternate equivalent question should be supplied. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=5c2c8c4b99931b1cc791ac09768c3eed7420f9a3&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
